Q: How can I allow <input type="file"> to accept only image files? A:

If you want to upload multiple images at once, you can add the multiple attribute to input:

<input type="file" multiple accept='image/*'>

upload multiple files: <input type="file" multiple accept='image/*'>

Q: Batch file that keeps the 7 latest files in a folder A:

If you don't write DOS scripts frequently which I don't, here is a summation of what others noted. Other examples here will need the batch file in the same folder that you're deleting from. To delete from another path: (Notice you have to add the path twice to the search and to the delete)

SET targetDir="C:\Test\Files\"
for /f "skip=7 eol=: delims=" %%F in ('dir /b /o-d /a-d %targetDir%*.txt') do @del "%targetDir%""%%F"

Thanks @dbenham, @SmileyFace, @user2924127 and all others who helped bring the answers.

Q: how to get the deepest layer of html A:

Now that we see you have guarantees about the nature of the input, it makes this task a lot easier. You don’t need an actual HTML parser. You just need to read the URL’s content, line by line, using a BufferedReader. Since you haven’t included any code, we don’t know if you have ever opened a URL or used the BufferedReader class before. We don’t even know if you’re familiar with String methods like startsWith.

Q: Sorting y axis of a graph based on frequencies of three discrete criteria in ggplot A:

Is this your expected outcome? Could this approach be adapted to suit?

library(tidyverse)

# for reproducability
set.seed(1234)

# create empty dataset
d <- data.frame(id = NULL,
                present = NULL)

# create data: nine subjects with forty observations each of a variable called 'present', with differing frequencies of three different discrete variables
for(i in 0:8) {
  d[i*40+(1:40), "present"] <- sample(x = c("no","yes","missing"),
                                      size = 40,
                                      prob = c(0.25, 0.4, 0.35),
                                      replace = T)
  d[i*40+(1:40), "id"] <- rep(paste0("id0",1+i),40)
}

# sort order of occurrence of the three levels of 'present'
d %>%
  group_by(id, present) %>%
  count %>%
  uncount(weights = n) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  tibble::add_column(obsNum = rep(1:40,times = 9)) -> d


d %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(row_order = 3 * sum(present == "missing") +
           2 * sum(present == "no") +
           1 * sum(present == "yes")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = obsNum, 
                       y = fct_reorder(id, -row_order),
                       colour = present)) +
  geom_point(shape = 15) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("yellow",
                                 "red",
                                 "black")) +
  labs(x = "observation number")

Q: Getting mypy to recognize tuple of certain length A:

Starting in version 1.7, mypy supports narrowing tuples using len checks. (This was part of PR #16237.) Thus, you can just throw a quick assertion into your function:

T_day = int | None
T_week = tuple[T_day, T_day, T_day, T_day, T_day, T_day, T_day]

def shift_week(dayofweek: int, week: T_week) -> T_week:
    week_shifted: list[T_day] = []
    week_shifted.extend(week[dayofweek:])
    week_shifted.extend(week[:dayofweek])
    rt = tuple(week_shifted)
    assert len(rt) == 7
    return rt
